name: the browse steps offset by the limit, not by the releases returned
why: The Web Service caps a release browse at 500 tracks, so a page can hold fewer than 100 releases; stepping by the limit then skips the ones it left out (the spec's first page has 90: offset 100 loses ten).
grep: every release, paged by the releases returned

name: the window reads only the first page
why: The window's point is every release. Here the guard is covered by another: _rgWindowFor() asks again on every repaint for a list that holds only its first page (firstPageOnly), so with the load loop cut after one page each repaint reads the next one, and the window still ends with all 150. Recorded so the overlap is known, not assumed.
grep: every release, paged by the releases returned

name: the window does not look up the group's facts
why: Type, rating, genres, links and annotation come from the one lookup made on pin.
grep: every release, paged by the releases returned

name: a card load running at the pin does not go on for the window
why: When Space comes before the card's first page has answered, the window joins that load and marks it all-pages. The spec pins only after the card has its page (its premise asserts the card's count first), so the load is never running at the pin: no spec here can see this guard. Recorded so the gap is known.
grep: every release, paged by the releases returned

name: this release is not first
why: The card and the window open with the page's own release first and marked.

name: a cover is asked for every release
why: Only cover-art-archive.front says the archive has a front; asking for the rest costs the archive a request each and shows nothing.
grep: covers only where the archive has a front

name: empty values sort first
why: An undated release says nothing about order; it goes last either way.

name: the subheader card waits for Ctrl
why: The link's card was never Ctrl-gated and stays on a plain hover (org/iframe.org, answer 8); only the "#" cell waits for Ctrl.
grep: a plain hover, beside the link

name: the "#" window steps nowhere
why: ← → step down the "#" column, from one sub-table into the next.
grep: Space pins, ← → step down the column

name: a no-match window shows the closest titles without links
why: The card cannot be clicked; the window is where the closest groups become reachable.
grep: closest titles and the search, as links

name: the Live page view's root is #content
why: _dpIsolateFrame() hides every sibling of the root and of its ancestors: #content would hide the sidebar (cover, rating, tags, links) along with the site's header and footer; #page hides only those (org/iframe.org R6).
grep: Live page: the release group page

name: a tap on a "#" cell is served by no source
why: A touch screen has no hover and no Ctrl: the tap is the only way to the window. Planted in the "#" source's resolve(), so the engine's own tap rule (pinned by detail-preview.json) stays as it is.
